quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a:
questions.explanation: A red flashing traffic light means the same thing as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop and then go when it is safe.

questions.question: Pennant-shaped signs tell you:
questions.explanation: Pennant-shaped signs mark no passing zones. Text on the sign will also say it is a no passing zone.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection when the light turns solid yellow. You should:

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and go through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a solid yellow light, slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane road with traffic in both directions, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane road, you must cross into the oncoming traffic lane to pass. Only pass if it is safe and legal to do so.

questions.question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, look:
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Know that tinted windows reduce visibility at night.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Looking into oncoming headlights causes your eyes to adjust and then take time to readjust when the car passes. During this time, you cannot see the road clearly.

questions.question: You are charged with driving under the influence and you refuse to take a chemical test. You may lose your license for 12 months:

options.text: Only if you are convicted of driving under the influence.
Only if you are convicted of a traffic violation.

questions.explanation: By driving, you agree to take a chemical test if asked by police. Refusing the test results in a license suspension for at least one year.

questions.question: An advisory speed sign:

options.text: Can be ignored in rainy, snowy, or icy conditions.
Shows a suggested speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shows a suggested speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Signs on curves and turns show a recommended speed for those areas. You should follow this speed even if the weather is good. In rain, snow, or ice, drive even slower than the recommended speed.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, you should:

options.text: Go slowly while you wait for an opening.
Speed up faster than the traffic.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic so you can merge smoothly and safely. You must give way to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand extended downward is a hand signal meaning:
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm downward, they are signaling they will stop. Adjust your driving if you see this signal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells you to keep right. It warns you about a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, what should you do?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: Which statement about work zones is true?

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as mobile equipment or snow removal. Work zones use orange signs with black letters. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up even with the car in front of your desired parking space.
questions.explanation: First, stop your car parallel to the car in front of the space you want. Then signal and turn your wheel to park.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what should worry you most?

options.text: Driving with your headlights out of alignment because one side of your car is higher than the other.
Damaging a tire from drifting onto the shoulder.
Hydroplaning, if the shoulder has water on it.
Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing control of the vehicle if you drift onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: This sign means the shoulder is lower than the road. If a wheel drops onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or steer sharply. This can cause you to lose control.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.
Signal at least 500 feet before your lane change when driving on residential streets.

questions.explanation: Always look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Signal 100 feet before turning on residential streets. Signal five seconds before changing lanes on a freeway.

questions.question: A speed limit sign is posted on a freeway exit ramp. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to this speed before entering the deceleration lane.
Regard the posted limit as only a suggestion.
Never drive slower than the posted speed on the exit ramp.
Slow to the posted speed once entering the exit ramp.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to the posted speed once entering the exit ramp.
questions.explanation: Keep your speed until you enter the exit ramp. Then slow down smoothly. Treat exit ramp speed limits like any other speed limit sign.

questions.question: When towing a trailer, what must you ensure?

options.text: The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the trailer hitch.
The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the vehicle's bumper.
The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the frame of the towing vehicle.
The trailer hitch is equipped with a fail-safe latch.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer has a safety chain securely attached to the frame of the towing vehicle.
questions.explanation: Safety chains must connect the trailer to the frame of the towing vehicle. Do not attach them to the trailer hitch.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel too far in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward oncoming traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
Let go of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Turn the steering wheel in the same direction the back of your car is sliding.

questions.question: When towing a trailer, how much of the trailer's weight should rest on your vehicle's hitch?
questions.explanation: About 10 to 15 percent of the trailer's weight should be on the hitch. Poor weight distribution makes it hard to control your vehicle and trailer.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is reasonable for the situation.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must follow posted speed limits and drive at a reasonable speed. Adjust your speed based on traffic, weather, road quality, light, and pedestrians. Always drive safely for current conditions.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system is dangerous because it can cause:
questions.explanation: Your exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak lets poisonous carbon monoxide into the cabin. Fix any leaks right away.

questions.question: What do round signs warn you about?
questions.explanation: Round signs warn drivers about upcoming railroad crossings. Be extra careful when you see this sign.

questions.question: You are waiting in an intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights to tell drivers to let you through.
Drive around the back of a car that is in your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting. If a car hits you from behind, straight wheels prevent you from being pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in fog, rain, or snow.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than traffic to get ahead.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Entrance ramps have acceleration lanes. Signal, look for an opening, speed up to match traffic, and merge safely into that opening.

questions.question: Which one does NOT affect how far it takes to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance. These change based on speed and road conditions.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare you for upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a stop sign is coming, so be ready to stop completely.
